prompts.dragon: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one production game sprite sheet, four painted poses of ONE original dark-fantasy dragon. Transparent background. Exact 2 by 2 equal square grid with generous empty gutters, no dividers or text. In each cell same complete ash-black and oxidized bronze scaled dragon, huge leathery ochre wings, heavy hooked muzzle, ember throat, long tail, no rider. Three-quarter side view facing RIGHT, camera 25 degrees above, orthographic dungeon game view. Top left: calm airborne wings raised partly, all claws tucked. Top right: powerful wingbeat wings spread horizontally, legs tucked. Bottom left: head extended in a fire-breathing attack pose with bright throat, no flame plume outside body. Bottom right: slain, wings folded and body collapsed on the ground. Same anatomy, body scale and lighting across four poses, all wings and tail entirely inside its own cell. Rich hand-painted oil rendering with crisp outer contour and broad readable value planes suitable for scaling small, no pixel art, no outline strokes, no ground shadows or scene. The dragon should read threatening and substantial at 40 game units tall; avoid tiny texture noise.
prompts.spider: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one four-pose game sprite atlas for a single giant cave-spider broodmother, dark fantasy painted dungeon game. True transparent background, exact two columns by two rows, generous gutters. Each cell contains the whole spider completely separated. Camera orthographic three-quarter overhead 30 degrees, faces RIGHT. Same broad bone-white hairy abdomen, dark umber chitin armor and eight long jointed legs, venom-teal mouth parts. Top left: low alert stance. Top right: rearing threat stance, front two legs raised. Bottom left: lunging bite, front legs extended, mouth exposed. Bottom right: dead curled legs beneath its body. Consistent body proportions and size, same subdued warm upper-left light. Readable bold silhouette and sharp painted edges, high quality hand-painted surfaces, subtle mottling, strong separation of ivory abdomen from dark legs. No floor, shadow, scenery, labels, grid lines, halos or pixel art. Separate real creature silhouettes, not four icons in frames.
prompts.spider_edit: Edit the just-generated four-pose spider sprite sheet. Keep each spider's anatomy, poses, colors, detailed painting and entire legs exactly as they are. Remove ALL the brown cloudy backdrop, halos, haze and shadows between and around the spiders, including inside every gap between legs, leaving only the four isolated creature cutouts on a fully transparent background. No replacement background, no glow. Make the creature bodies opaque and their edges crisply antialiased. Preserve full legs; maintain the separated four-pose layout.
prompts.hunter: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one game NPC sprite, original wounded treasure hunter for painted dark fantasy dungeon. Full body, true transparent background. Weathered middle-aged human explorer in a faded wine-red padded coat and brown leather expedition harness, bandaged forehead and one bandaged leg, battered high boots, unlit belt lantern, rolled survey charts and climbing rope on pack. Leaning on a short walking staff with one hand held against injured ribs. Tired but determined face. Three-quarter side view facing right, orthographic camera about 20 degrees overhead. Cohesive hand-painted rendering, clear garment planes, crisp silhouette and edges, no pixel art. Warm-neutral daylight without dramatic cast shadows. Entire staff, boots and head within the frame, isolated cutout with plenty of blank transparent margin. No floor, ground shadow, fog, backdrop, lettering or frame.
prompts.timber: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: seamless square top-down wooden dungeon platform material texture for a painted dark fantasy game. Fill the whole square edge to edge with broad weathered chestnut oak planks running horizontally, cross-grain cracks, subtle abrasion and a few blunt forged iron nail heads. True orthographic top-down flat surface, not a perspective object. Planks are securely joined with slender dark seams, tan worn upper faces and warm brown recessed seams. Restrained detail, broad legible boards, gentle color variation, medium-light value so safe walkable flooring contrasts clearly against a nearly black abyss. No broken holes, no gaps big enough to fall through, no railings, rope, objects, borders, shadows, text, perspective or vignette. Hand-painted realism, no pixel art. Tileable across every edge.
prompts.hoard: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one transparent cutout treasure-hoard scenery asset for a painted dark fantasy dungeon game. A low, broad mound of old gold coins with tarnished gilt goblets, jeweled crowns and two half-buried ironbound treasure chests, a few emeralds/rubies as color accents. Wide horizontal silhouette about 7:4, orthographic three-quarter view from above at 35 degrees. Warm gold with restrained bright edges, strong simple masses that read at small scale. Entire hoard visible, generous transparent margin. Painterly realistic surfaces with crisp contours, no pixel art. No floor, walls, background, shadow cloud, dragons, people, magical barrier, glow halo, symbols, labels or text. Ground-contact base is broad and horizontal. This is scenery under separately drawn game loot, not an inventory icon.
prompts.map: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent inventory icon for an original painted dark fantasy game, one expedition map. A small folded ochre parchment chart partly unfolded, its corners curled, with a simple charcoal sketch of wooden bridges over a circular abyss and a little red dragon-head seal at one corner. Leather thong and small tarnished brass compass resting on the map. Entire object, orthographic three-quarter overhead view, centered on fully transparent background with generous empty margin. Clear bold silhouette and warm parchment mass that reads at 64px, crisp hand-painted edges, no pixel art, no written letters, no numbers, no captions, no decorative border, no background, no external shadow.
